newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end higher, fight off Heineken blues.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end higher, fight off Heineken blues.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Monday, shaking off the gloom cast by another fall in Heineken and a heavy ex-dividend dip in Royal Dutch to climb in the last hour of business in line with Wall Street.
"The market is still pretty shaken up by the Heineken figures last Friday and the warning about lower profits -- you can see the impact of that in the index," said one dealer.

The AEX index of 25 leading Dutch shares finished 2.12 points higher at 568.17, moving ahead after a mainly mixed session as Wall Street built on Friday's record high close with double figure gains in early Monday trading.

"The market would have been a lot higher if the Heineken factor wasn't there and Royal Dutch wasn't ex-dividend," said one dealer, calculating that together the two had shaved about two points off the day's rise.

"With another two points on the AEX by the close our rise today would have been in line with the other bourses in Europe," he said, adding the renewed Wall Street gain and firmer bond prices had encouraged investors around the region.

A fresh round of analysts' downgrades pushed Heineken 19.50 guilders lower to a close of 303.00, making a 16.5 percent fall since last week's results and profit-warning trauma. The shares touched a seven month low of 294.00 during the session.

Heineken shares were again among the most active, although with 1.3 million traded by the close business had died down from Friday's sell-off when over 3.7 million changed hands, well up from the more normal daily turnover of 200,000 to 400,000.
The Heineken fall-out had a positive side effect for Unilever, up 5.80 guilders to 269.80. "People are switching out of Heineken into Unilever," said a dealer.

"Unilever has of course been on the run higher for the last few days after the news about pushing out the products that aren't performing that well," he added. "They've been busy with road shows in the U.S. and that's pushing things along nicely."
